source_evidence: If you take all or part of your money out during the surrender period, you may have to pay a surrender charge. The surrender period is a set period of time that typically lasts six to ten years, or even longer, after you purchase the annuity. Surrender charges will reduce the value and the return of your investment.
question: What can happen if you withdraw money from an indexed annuity during its surrender period?
answer: You may have to pay a surrender charge, which reduces the value of your annuity and the return on your investment. Check your contract to understand when its surrender period applies.
